note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Several months of low mood, low appetite, low energy/fatigue; intermittent palpitations and subjective shortness of breath; intermittent nausea; unintentional weight loss.
- Onset/duration/progression:
  - Low mood and low energy: "long, long ago" — worsened over months; began/changed after moving to a new law firm ~3–3.5 months ago.
  - Appetite loss began ~3–3.5 months ago; weight loss ~1 stone over ~6 months.
  - Palpitations/shortness of breath: episodic, notably in lifts/when feeling unwell; not exertional (patient can walk ~1 mile without dyspnea).
  - Nausea intermittent, no vomiting.
- Associated symptoms/context: headaches occasionally; relationship/sexual activity affected per patient ("wife was starting to complain"); reduced physical activity recently.
- GI/Bowel: bowel habits reported as normal; no diarrhoea, no blood or mucus.
- Red flags denied/absent: no chest pain, no vomiting, no haematemesis/rectal bleeding reported.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid).
- Thyroxine: prior use reported; patient stopped taking thyroxine since changing GP — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Not recorded.
- Other chronic illnesses/hospitalizations: Not recorded.
- Medications (other than thyroxine): Not recorded.
- Recent investigations: No recent blood tests; patient reports none in a long time.

Physical Examination:
- Physical exam performed: Not recorded / no formal examination done during this consult.
- Reported or observed findings (patient-reported):
  - Episodic palpitations with sensation of rapid heartbeat.
  - Subjective shortness of breath during episodes (particularly in lifts); no exertional SOB.
  - Intermittent nausea; headaches.
  - Weight loss ~1 stone over ~6 months.
  - Bowel movements painless and normal.
- Relevant negatives (patient-reported):
  - No chest pain.
  - No diarrhoea, no blood or mucus in stool.
  - No vomiting.
- Vital signs: Not recorded.
- Mental status / orientation: Not recorded.

Impression:
- One-line clinical impression: Provisional depressive syndrome with fatigue and weight loss; differential includes thyroid dysfunction due to stopped thyroxine and situational anxiety/panic causing episodic palpitations.
- Top DDx consistent with transcript:
  1. Major depressive disorder — months of persistent low mood, low appetite, anergy, functional impact after job change.
  2. Thyroid dysfunction (undertreatment or other thyroid abnormality) — known hypothyroidism and patient stopped thyroxine; thyroid tests pending.
  3. Anxiety disorder / situational panic (possible situational triggers) — episodic palpitations and breathlessness notably in lifts.

Management Plan:
- Immediate/short-term:
  - Arrange a general set of blood tests (requested): Full blood count, renal function, liver function, thyroid function tests, vitamin levels (as discussed by clinician).
  - Patient instructed to call the service support number via the app to organize blood tests; clinician will complete required forms.
  - Patient will receive a text message when results are available prompting to book follow-up appointment.
  - No change to thyroxine prescribed in this consult; note patient stopped it — review after blood results (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Safety/urgent advice:
  - Advise attending A&E urgently for new or worsening chest pain, severe breathlessness, syncope, or acute deterioration.
  - Advise contacting the service sooner if symptoms worsen or new concerning features develop (change in bowel habits, vomiting, etc.).
- Further care actions:
  - If blood tests are normal, arrange a face-to-face physical examination and further assessment.
  - Consider mental health assessment/treatment options based on results and clinical follow-up (to be discussed at follow-up).

Patient Summary:
- Peter, 35, presents with months of low mood, low energy and appetite with ~1 stone weight loss over ~6 months after a job change, plus episodic palpitations/shortness of breath (worse in lifts) and intermittent nausea. He has a history of hypothyroidism but stopped taking thyroxine and has not had recent blood tests. Plan is to obtain general bloods (including thyroid tests), arrange further assessment based on results, and advise urgent care if chest pain or marked deterioration occurs.

Key Takeaways:
- Call the app support number to arrange the blood tests that were requested.
- Seek urgent care (A&E) for new or worsening chest pain, severe shortness of breath, syncope, or acute deterioration.
- Follow-up appointment will be arranged after blood results; do not wait if symptoms worsen.

Next Steps:
- Patient to call support via app to book blood tests.
- Perform blood tests: FBC, renal/liver profile, thyroid function tests, vitamin levels (as per clinician plan).
- Review blood results; book follow-up appointment (patient will receive text to book).
- If bloods are unrevealing, arrange face-to-face physical examination and further workup (per clinician).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature) — Not recorded.
  - Formal physical examination findings — Not recorded.
  - Medication details (current/other meds, exact thyroxine dose/route/frequency) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Allergies and medication intolerances — Not recorded.
  - Social history details: smoking, alcohol, substance use — Not recorded.
  - Formal mental health screening elements: sleep, suicidal ideation, anhedonia, concentration, duration specifics — Not recorded.
  - Family history — Not recorded.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted; DDx considerations are consistent with the transcript and clinician plan.
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversation overall intelligible but contained intermittent unclear/overlapping segments and some omitted patient responses; adequate for history-taking but lacks objective vitals and exam data.
